name: Paris, France 🇫🇷
subtitle: Bistros, boulangeries, and Michelin — the full Paris table
items: Du Pain et des Idées (Canal Saint-Martin, Isaac Correa — the croissant to benchmark all croissants)
Septime (11th, Bertrand Grébaut, 1-star — the modern Parisian bistro at its peak)
Frenchie (Sentier, Gregory Marchand — changed what a Paris wine bar could be)
Le Comptoir du Relais (Saint-Germain, Yves Camdeborde — Saturday night no-reservations prix fixe is a rite of passage)
Café de Flore (Saint-Germain — Sartre and Simone de Beauvoir's table, tourist or not)
Les Deux Magots (Saint-Germain — Hemingway's café, do it once)
Bouillon Chartier (9th, since 1896 — the original French canteen, queue, eat for €15)
Chez L'Ami Jean (7th, Stéphane Jégo, Basque — the riz au lait is legendary)
L'Ami Louis (3rd, since 1924 — controversial, expensive, chicken for two for €100+, cult status)
La Tour d'Argent (5th, since 1582 — the duck press, the Seine view, the history)
Pierre Gagnaire (8th, 3 Michelin stars — molecular but soulful)
Le Chateaubriand (11th, Inaki Aizpitarte, natural wine mecca)
David Toutain (7th, 2-star, the quiet one everyone serious talks about)
Brasserie Lipp (Saint-Germain, classic — choucroute garnie, period-correct)
Taillevent (8th, 2-star, the great classic)
Jacques Genin (Marais, best chocolate + caramel in Paris, tarte tatin on Sundays)
Verjus (1st, Braden Perkins + Laura Adrian, American expats — the best wine list)
L'Astrance (16th, Pascal Barbot, 3-star — tiny, rare, extraordinary)
Breizh Café (Marais, buckwheat crêpes — take the crêpe seriously here)
Café Procope (Saint-Germain, since 1686 — the world's oldest café still in operation)
